summary: Since a 2021 reform Iraq issues 60-day visas on arrival (about USD 77) to citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and a set of other countries; other nationalities must apply through an Iraqi embassy. The Kurdistan Region runs its own, broader entry regime whose stamps are not valid for federal Iraq.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Iraq.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

travelInsurance.text: Not checked at the border, but comprehensive insurance that explicitly covers Iraq (many policies exclude it) and medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

onwardTicket.text: Not formally required, but airlines and border officers may ask about your onward plans, accommodation and the purpose of your visit.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; carry enough US dollars in cash for your stay, as cards are of little use.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

currencyLimits.text: Cash worth USD 10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iraq

notes: Photography near checkpoints, government buildings and military sites is dangerous — always ask before photographing people or infrastructure.
Drones are effectively prohibited and will be confiscated.
Evidence of travel to Israel can lead to refusal of entry.

payments.text: Iraq is overwhelmingly cash-based. Bring US dollars (newer, undamaged notes) to exchange. Cards work only at a handful of upmarket hotels, and ATMs accepting foreign cards are scarce, though somewhat better in Erbil.

safety.text: Most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel to Iraq: terrorism, kidnapping and sudden unrest remain real risks, and checkpoints are everywhere. The Kurdistan Region is markedly calmer but not risk-free. If you go, travel with an experienced local operator and monitor advisories closely.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Iraq Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (March–April) and fall (October–November) avoid the ferocious summer, when temperatures can pass 50°C in Baghdad and the south.

idp.text: Iraq is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Iraq is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Iraq yet.

tips.text: The Kurdistan Region (Erbil, Sulaymaniyah) operates its own entry regime with a broader visa-on-arrival list, but a Kurdistan stamp is NOT valid for federal Iraq. Traveling from Erbil to Baghdad or Mosul requires a federal Iraqi visa; decide which regime you need before you fly.
Bring your whole budget in US dollars cash, in good condition — older or marked notes are refused. The visa-on-arrival fee itself (about USD 77) must be paid in cash.
Expect frequent checkpoints between cities. Carry your passport at all times, keep visa copies on your phone, and build waiting time into any road journey.
During Ashura and the Arbaeen pilgrimage, Karbala and Najaf receive millions of visitors — accommodation sells out and roads close. Dress conservatively at all religious sites year-round.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iraq?
faq.answer: Yes. Citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, China, Russia and Switzerland can obtain a 60-day visa on arrival (about USD 77, cash) under the 2021 reform. Everyone else must apply for a visa in advance at an Iraqi embassy, where approval can take several weeks.

faq.question: Is a visa for the Kurdistan Region the same as an Iraqi visa?
faq.answer: No. Kurdistan issues its own entry stamps at Erbil and Sulaymaniyah airports to a broader list of nationalities, but they are valid only inside the Kurdistan Region. A federal Iraqi visa (for example the airport visa on arrival in Baghdad, Basra or Najaf) is required for the rest of the country.

faq.question: Is Iraq safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Iraq remains a high-risk destination: most governments advise against all travel, or against all nonessential travel because of terrorism, kidnapping and unrest. That said, organized tourism to Baghdad, Babylon, the southern shrine cities and especially the Kurdistan Region has grown since 2021. Go with an experienced operator, expect checkpoints, and follow advisories.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Iraq?
faq.answer: No. Israeli passport holders are not admitted to Iraq, and Iraqi law criminalises contact that would normalise relations. Evidence of travel to Israel in another passport can also cause problems at the border.

faq.question: How do I pay for the Iraqi visa on arrival?
faq.answer: In cash, in US dollars — about USD 77. Bring clean, newer-series banknotes, as worn or older bills are frequently refused. Card payment is not reliably available at arrival halls.
